answer: Randomness-gated identity cap: each agent must solve a crystal-seeded puzzle whose seed is drawn from a public beacon after registration closes, so identities cannot be precomputed. The agent submits a pigment hash binding its key to the future seed. Only solutions below a threshold yield a valid identity slot, capping how many ties one actor can mint per round. An attacker pays compute plus forfeited slots for every extra identity, and the mesa of unused submissions costs him the full per-identity work with no resale value.
